title: Career Roadmap · Tailor
summary: A Tailor measures, cuts, stitches, alters and finishes garments to customer or production specifications, working independently, in tailoring shops or in garment manufacturing.

facts.Current degree: ITI Cutting & Sewing / Sewing Technology / Fashion Design & Technology / Embroidery

blocks.label: Recommended
blocks.text: Class 8 or 10 may be sufficient for relevant vocational routes; requirements vary by trade.

blocks.label: Stream
blocks.text: No specific Class 11–12 stream is generally required for entry-level tailoring.

blocks.label: Explore
blocks.text: Garment construction, fabrics, patterns, measurements, stitching and finishing.

blocks.label: Early skills
blocks.text: Hand stitching, machine operation, measurement accuracy, creativity and customer communication.

rows.text: Garment cutting, stitching, fitting and finishing
Garment design, pattern work and apparel production
Embroidery patterns and decorative garment work
Broader garment production, pattern development and quality roles

blocks.text: DGT currently lists Sewing Technology as a one-year trade with Class 8 entry, Dress Making as a one-year trade with Class 8 entry, and Fashion Design & Technology as a one-year trade with Class 10 entry. Verify current official notification.

blocks.label: Stage 1 — Foundation
blocks.text: Hand stitching, fabric types, measurements and sewing-machine safety.

blocks.label: Stage 2 — Core skills
blocks.text: Cutting, seams, zips, hems, sleeves and basic garment construction.

blocks.label: Stage 3 — Advanced skills
blocks.text: Pattern drafting, fitting, alterations, finishing and production quality.

blocks.label: Stage 4 — Career preparation
blocks.text: Build a garment portfolio, practise customer fittings and estimate fabric and labour costs.

blocks.label: Project ideas
blocks.text: Stitch a basic shirt or kurta • Create a measurement chart • Draft a simple pattern • Complete an alteration and finishing portfolio.

blocks.label: Industries
blocks.text: Tailoring shops, boutiques, apparel manufacturing, uniforms, fashion houses, garment exports and home-based tailoring services.

blocks.label: Technical skills
blocks.text: Accurate measurement, cutting, pattern reading, stitching, fitting, finishing, fabric identification and quality control.

blocks.label: Tools / technologies
blocks.text: Sewing machine, overlock machine, measuring tape, cutting tools, iron/pressing equipment and pattern-drafting tools.
Useful credentials

items.text: DGT / NCVT-recognized Sewing Technology, Dress Making or Fashion Design & Technology certificate.
Apprenticeship completion credential, where awarded.
Advanced pattern-making or garment-construction training.
Computer-aided embroidery or apparel-design training for specialization.

blocks.text: Practical garment samples and consistent finishing quality are important evidence of skill; certificates do not guarantee employment.

blocks.label: Countries to explore
blocks.text: Italy, UK, Canada, Australia and Germany.
Institutions / routes to investigate

items.text: Politecnico di Milano — Italy; fashion-design programs.
London College of Fashion, University of the Arts London — UK; fashion and garment-related study.
George Brown College — Canada; fashion-related programs, subject to current offerings.
TAFE providers — Australia; fashion, clothing production and textile-related courses.
German vocational / applied-science institutions — textile, clothing technology and apparel pathways.

blocks.text: These are research starting points, not confirmation of current course availability or entry eligibility.

blocks.label: Common requirements
blocks.text: Academic records, language proficiency where applicable, course-specific prerequisites and portfolio work for some fashion-design programs. Verify current international admissions and tuition directly with each institution.

blocks.label: Roles
blocks.text: Tailor, Alterations Specialist, Sample Machinist, Sewing Machine Operator and Garment Production Assistant.

blocks.label: Industries
blocks.text: Clothing alterations, fashion, costume production, apparel manufacturing, hospitality uniforms and textiles.
Demand, pay, qualification recognition and work authorization vary by country. Employment and visa sponsorship are not guaranteed.
